about.title: San Juan Bautista Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: San Juan Bautista is a small city, but its mission-town streets, agricultural roads, and stretches of SR-156 see plenty of work-related travel — delivery drivers, farm crews, contractors, and service workers moving through daily. When a job injury happens here, California's workers' compensation system usually covers medical bills and lost wages regardless of fault, but that system doesn't always tell the whole story. If a subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to the harm, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your workers' comp benefits. Local crash data shows collisions on corridors like Rt 156 and SR-156 Westbound, some of which involve people working at the time. LawProactive is a free service — we don't practice law ourselves, but we can connect you with an independent attorney who can look at whether a third party bears responsibility for your injury.

whyChoose.title: Why People Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding Your Options Beyond Workers' Comp
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually your exclusive remedy against your employer, but if a third party like a subcontractor or another driver contributed to your injury, a separate claim may be available. An independent attorney can help sort out which path applies to your situation.

items.title: Protecting You From Retaliation
items.desc: California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting a workplace injury. If you're worried about your job while dealing with an injury, an attorney can explain your rights before you take any next steps.

items.title: Watching the Clock on Deadlines
items.desc: Workplace injuries generally need to be reported to your employer within 30 days, and any third-party injury claim carries its own 2-year filing deadline. Missing either window can limit your options, so timing matters.

items.question: I was hurt driving for work near SR-156 in San Juan Bautista — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: Often both paths apply: workers' compensation typically covers your medical care and lost wages regardless of fault, while a separate claim against another driver or negligent party may be possible if they contributed to the crash. An independent attorney can review the details of your San Juan Bautista incident and explain how the two interact. LawProactive can connect you with someone free of charge to sort this out.

items.question: How soon do I need to report my workplace injury?
items.answer: California generally requires you to notify your employer within 30 days of the injury to preserve your workers' compensation rights. Waiting longer can complicate your claim, so it's best to report as soon as you're able. If a third party is also involved, that claim carries a separate 2-year deadline.

items.question: Can my employer punish me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No — retaliation against an employee for reporting a workplace injury is illegal under California law. If you're facing pushback at work after getting hurt, an independent attorney can advise you on protecting your job and your claim at the same time.
